'''''Cephalaria leucantha''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]]s in the family [[Caprifoliaceae]].<ref>[https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Taxonomy/Browser/wwwtax.cgi?lin=s&p=has_linkout&id=183559 NCBI]</ref>

==Description==
''Cephalaria leucantha'' grows to {{convert|90|-|150|cm}} in height. This hardy [[perennial plant|perennial]] plant has a long stem with divided, fern-like leaves. It produces white or pale lemon flowers from July to November.<ref>[http://www.plant-world-seeds.com/store/view_seed_item/304 Plant World]</ref>

==Distribution==
This species is present in northern Africa and in southern Europe (Albania, former Yugoslavia, Greece, Italy, France, Portugal, and Spain).<ref>{{GRIN | accessdate = 23 January 2018}}</ref>

==History==
The species was described as ''Scabiosa trenta'' by [[Belsazar Hacquet]] in 1782. This resulted in a century-long search by other botanists to find the new species that Hacquet had described in the [[Julian Alps]]. It was not until 1893 that the Austrian botanist [[Anton Kerner von Marilaun]] determined that Hacquet's species was actually ''Cephalaria leucantha'', which is now extinct in the Julian Alps.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kerner |first1=Anton |title=Scabiosa Trenta Hacquet |journal=Österreichische Botanische Zeitschrift |date=1893 |volume=43 |pages=113–117}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |author1=Matej Župančič |author2=Stanko Flego |editor1-last=Flego |editor1-first=Stanko |editor2-last=Rupel |editor2-first=Lidija |title=Ludwig Karl Moser (1845–1918) med Dunajem in Trstom |date=2012 |publisher=Založba ZRC |location=Ljubljana |page=198 |chapter=Non ad personam sed ad rem (ali o kačjem pastirju in želvi)}}</ref>
